editorial.headline: The Clear Limits of Commercial Clothes Alterations in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Commercial clothes alterations are nationally open to full foreign ownership, but a PT PMA cannot register this activity in Bali.
editorial.body:
Commercial clothes alteration is a practical service with a precise legal perimeter: altering garments for the general public as a commercial activity. It covers a business that takes in clothing from everyday customers and returns it altered. The emphasis is on the paid public-facing service itself, not a vague label for any work connected with clothing. That clarity gives the activity its useful, modest definition: a commercial alterations desk serving the public.

The record opens registration at the Mikro, Kecil and Menengah scales. These are not background details. They describe the operating sizes available to the activity and help explain its place in the business landscape: it is structured for micro, small and medium enterprise participation. A founder considering this activity should read the scale line together with the scope line. The public-service character and the permitted scales belong to the same picture, setting the terms on which the activity is presented for registration.

At the national level, foreign investment has a clean answer. The activity is TERBUKA for PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain English, the national record permits a foreign investor to hold the whole business. There is no need to soften that finding or to imply a national cap that the record does not contain. But a national ceiling is only one layer of the picture for a Bali venture.

In Bali, the operative conclusion is different: a foreign investor cannot register this activity there today. The Bali status is Closed to PMA (no Besar scale). The reason is structural: OSS provides no Usaha Besar scale row, leaving the activity reserved for UMKM; a PT PMA is, by law, Usaha Besar and therefore cannot register it. The record also identifies a permanent, island-wide Bali PMA block for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The result is direct rather than nuanced: national foreign openness does not translate into Bali registration for a PT PMA. An enterprise that wants to serve the public through commercial clothing alterations in Bali must take that local registration barrier as the deciding fact.
editorial.pullQuote: National foreign openness does not translate into Bali registration for a PT PMA.
